title: Leo's train adventure to the doctor
label: Blood test

friend.name: Choo the Train
friend.look: a cute toy train with a big smile and a blue body

plan.label: Needles or shots
helps: sit up on the grown-up's lap in a comfort hug instead of lying down
look at a video, bubbles, or a toy during the poke
know it hurts for about 2 seconds, then it is over
ask: numbing cream about an hour before
a cold or vibrating device on the arm (like Buzzy)
doing it sitting up, in a comfort hold
counting down "3, 2, 1" only if the child likes that

plan.label: Being away from me
helps: the grown-up stays in the room
know when the grown-up will be back, with a picture
ask: staying with the child the whole time
being there when anesthesia starts and when the child wakes up

pages.text: I go to the clinic. I see trains outside.
pages.say: Hmm... hello, Leo! It's me, Choo the Train! [excited] Today... the doctor! You and me. Here we go!
pages.scene: A smiling receptionist behind a bright clinic front desk greets the child and their grown-up, with Choo the Train beside them.

pages.text: I wait. I have my blue blanket.
pages.say: Ooooh! Look, Leo! The blue blanket. The soft blue blanket! Can you hold it?
pages.scene: The child sits with their grown-up in a waiting room, holding the blue blanket, and Choo the Train is on their lap.

pages.text: I sit in a chair. It has an armrest.
pages.say: Ahhh! What is that? The chair. The big chair! It goes up... up... up! Can you see it?
pages.scene: The child sits in a big chair with an armrest, and Choo the Train is beside them, also sitting in a tiny chair.

pages.text: A band goes on my arm. It feels tight.
pages.say: Oh my! Look! The band. The stretchy band! Can you feel it?
pages.scene: A nurse puts a stretchy band on the child's arm, while the child holds their blue blanket and Choo the Train looks on.

pages.text: I feel worried. My grown-up is here.
pages.say: Psst... Leo. It is OK to feel worried. I am here. Your grown-up is here.
pages.scene: The child looks worried, holding their blue blanket, and Choo the Train gives a reassuring look, while the grown-up comforts them.

pages.text: The nurse shows me a needle. It is small.
pages.say: Hmm... what do I see? The needle. The little needle! Can you see it?
pages.scene: The nurse shows the child a needle, while the child holds their blue blanket and Choo the Train looks on.

pages.say: Psst... Leo. Now the poke. A sharp poke. It hurts for 2 seconds. One... two... done! I'm right here. Squeeze your grown-up's hand.
pages.scene: The nurse gives the child a shot, while the child sits on the grown-up's lap, holding the blue blanket, and Choo the Train is beside them.

pages.text: Tubes fill up. It takes a minute.
pages.say: Ooooh! Look! The tubes. The little tubes! Can you see them fill up?
pages.scene: The child watches as small tubes fill up with blood, while holding their blue blanket and Choo the Train looks on.

pages.text: I get a bandage. It is sticky.
pages.say: Ahhh! What is that? The bandage. The sticky bandage! Can you feel it?
pages.scene: The nurse puts a bandage on the child's arm, while the child holds their blue blanket and Choo the Train looks on.

pages.text: The visit is over. I can play trains.
pages.say: Hmm... all done! Now we play trains! Choo choo! Can you make train sounds?
pages.scene: The child plays with toy trains, with Choo the Train beside them, and the grown-up smiles.

pages.text: I go home. I am happy.
pages.say: Ooooh! Look, Leo! We're going home! You and me. Here we go! [excited]
pages.scene: The child and their grown-up leave the clinic, with Choo the Train beside them, and the child holds their blue blanket.
